saints.name: St. Catherine Labouré
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: The humble Daughter of Charity to whom Our Lady entrusted the Miraculous Medal…
biography: Born in Burgundy in 1806, Catherine Labouré entered the Daughters of Charity of St. Vincent de Paul in Paris. In 1830, in the convent chapel of the Rue du Bac, she received a series of apparitions of the Blessed Virgin Mary, who asked that a medal be struck according to the image she showed — the medal that became known as the Miraculous Medal.

Keeping her role as visionary hidden, she spent the next forty-six years in obscurity, humbly caring for the aged and the sick at a hospice on the edge of Paris. Only after her death in 1876 was her identity widely known. Canonized in 1947, she is remembered for her hiddenness and her devotion to Our Lady.
saints.knownFor: The apparitions that gave the Church the Miraculous Medal.
